text:
Poland signed a five-year deal worth around $300 million with U.S. tech giant Palantir on Friday to expand the use of artificial intelligence across its armed forces.
Warsaw’s decision to adopt Palantir’s Maven system, already used by Ukraine and NATO, comes as European militaries grapple with how to strengthen their defenses against Russia while reducing their reliance on American technology.
“It would be stupid and wrong not to use it,” Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told reporters, crediting Palantir’s technology with helping Ukraine withstand more than four years of fighting Russia.
Maven uses AI to analyze military data, supporting everything from logistics to the identification of battlefield targets.
Palantir celebrated the deal on X, calling Maven “the vanguard of next-generation AI warfare” and saying it was proud to stand with Poland in defending a “sovereign Europe.”
The company, which has drawn criticism for its work with U.S. immigration authorities and the Israeli military, faced protests in Warsaw earlier this month over concerns about data security and technological independence.
“All the keys, servers and information are — and will remain — exclusively in the possession of the Polish Armed Forces,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.
Defense authorities in Denmark, Finland, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and Sweden already use Palantir software , though not all use Maven.
Some are seeking to reduce that dependence. The Dutch military said in late October it wanted a European alternative by 2028, while France and Germany agreed in July to explore developing their own defense software.
Kosiniak-Kamysz said he would have chosen a Polish supplier had one offered comparable technology, suggesting Poland could develop its own alternative by the time the contract expires.
